title_en: You must get at least the minimum wage, on time
law: Code on Wages, 2019, Sections 5, 17 and 45 (in force from 21 November 2025 under Gazette notification S.O. 5322(E); it repealed the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the Minimum Wages Act, 1948)
rule_plain: Your employer must not pay you less than the minimum wage set by the government. If you are paid every month, you must get your pay before the 7th day of the next month. If you are removed from the job or you resign, you must get your wages within two working days.
what_you_can_do: You can file a claim for your unpaid wages with the claims authority that the government appoints.
A trade union you belong to, or the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, can also file the claim.
File the claim within three years from the day the claim arises.
where_to_get_help: The claims authority appointed under Section 45 of the Code on Wages, 2019, or the Inspector-cum-Facilitator.
